chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Harun ibn Harizah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would eat the eating of a servant and sit the sitting of a servant, and he knew that he was a servant.

key_terms.وَيَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ عَبْدٌ: and he knew that he was a servant
key_terms.يَأْكُلُ أَكْلَ الْعَبْدِ: eating the eating of a servant
key_terms.يَجْلِسُ جِلْسَةَ الْعَبْدِ: sitting the sitting of a servant

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad demonstrate humility through his daily habits?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the Prophet’s (PBUH) embodiment of *tawadu* (humility), demonstrating that his divine status did not preclude him from adopting the simple, unpretentious habits of a servant. This serves as a practical model for the Shia tradition, emphasizing that true leadership involves accessibility and modesty in daily conduct, reinforcing the concept that prophetic authority is rooted in servitude to God rather than worldly elevation.
